definition: Fun-seeking is a component of the behavioral activation system that reflects sensitivity to rewarding, positively reinforcing experiences. In this study context, higher fun-seeking was linked with greater risk of risky single-occasion drinking and alcohol use disorder, partly through motives to enhance positive feelings.

reasons: The first sentence goes beyond the packet by defining fun-seeking as “sensitivity to rewarding, positively reinforcing experiences”; the source only identifies fun seeking as a BAS facet and does not explicitly define it that way.
The wording “behavioral activation system” and the reward-sensitivity description are generalized from the broader BAS framework rather than specifically supported for fun-seeking in the packet.

The definition’s first sentence states that fun-seeking “reflects sensitivity to rewarding, positively reinforcing experiences,” but the packet only describes BAS as including “fun seeking, drive, reward responsiveness” as distinct neurobiological systems, and does not explicitly define fun-seeking in terms of sensitivity to rewarding/positively reinforcing experiences.

The definition frames the term within the field “diagnosis,” but the packet presents fun-seeking as part of reinforcement sensitivity linked to alcohol misuse outcomes (e.g., risky single-occasion drinking and alcohol use disorder), not as a diagnostic concept or diagnostic criterion.
